learning: If the metrics again match iterations 0 to 3 to four decimals, the pipeline is the likely blocker and no further geometry should be tested until it is checked. If they differ, the next test is whether the larger radius makes the existing kp too strong or too weak for the new yaw response.
notes: Diagnostic package: the controller is held at iteration-3 gains so that wheel_radius 0.04 m is the only change. Metrics should differ if the pipeline is live. Expect a shift in progress and completion_time first.
rationale: Iterations 0 to 3 produced identical race metrics to four decimals on every track (score 26.0449, one line-loss event per trial, max_error 0.0609 to 0.0614 m, no finishes), across changes to spread, footprint, weight scaling and wheel_track. That pattern suggests the race pipeline may be repeating one result, so this package keeps the controller fixed to isolate the geometry change. The Builder's iteration 4 geometry changes only wheel_radius from 0.03 m to 0.04 m, with sensors, footprint, wheel_track 0.10 m, body and mass unchanged. For this geometry I keep the iteration-3 controller exactly: base_speed 1.6, kp 2.0, ki 0.0, kd 0.05, sensor_weights (-1.5, -0.75, 0, 0.75, 1.5) matching x/0.02 scaling, and line_loss last_direction. A larger wheel radius raises ground speed per PWM by about 33 percent and also raises the wheel-speed difference per unit turn, so yaw response per turn command should rise. I expect the speed and yaw changes to show up in progress and completion_time first. I have no measured evidence for a different gain, so I do not change kp or kd now. The full observation set is kept so the first line-loss point and the first off-track step can be located if the race responds.
